security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD kernel (S-mode) executes a CSR read or write to stimecmp when menvcfg.STCE=0 — either because OpenSBI/boot firmware never set the STCE bit, or because M-mode software dynamically cleared it. The resulting illegal-instruction exception is fatal in kernel mode.
security_spec.summary: S-mode direct stimecmp access traps fatally when menvcfg.STCE=0; FreeBSD must gate stimecmp usage on STCE probe before touching the CSR

findings.finding: FreeBSD S-mode kernel writes to stimecmp CSR guarded only by has_sstc (derived from ISA string parsing), without verifying menvcfg.STCE is set by M-mode firmware. Per spec (machine.adoc:2233-2235), when menvcfg.STCE=0, any non-M-mode access to stimecmp raises an illegal-instruction exception, which is fatal in kernel mode. If M-mode firmware advertises Sstc in ISA string but fails to set or later clears menvcfg.STCE, the kernel panics.

spec_citations.excerpt: The Sstc extension adds the STCE (STimecmp Enable) bit to menvcfg CSR. The STCE bit enables stimecmp for S-mode when set to one. When this extension is implemented and STCE in menvcfg is zero, an attempt to access stimecmp in a mode other than M-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception

This extension serves to provide supervisor mode with its own CSR-based timer interrupt facility that it can directly manage to provide its own timer service (in the form of having its own stimecmp register). This extension adds the STCE bit to the menvcfg and henvcfg CSRs.

findings.finding: Timer interrupt handler writes to stimecmp CSR (writing -1UL to disable the timer interrupt) guarded by the same has_sstc flag. Same vulnerability as set_timecmp: if menvcfg.STCE is not actually set by M-mode, the csr_write(stimecmp, -1UL) will cause a fatal illegal-instruction exception in the interrupt handler context.

spec_citations.excerpt: When this extension is implemented and STCE in menvcfg is zero, an attempt to access stimecmp in a mode other than M-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception

findings.finding: has_sstc is derived from ISA string parsing (SV_SSTC bit in smode_extensions), not from reading menvcfg.STCE. FreeBSD runs in S-mode and cannot read menvcfg directly. The ISA string advertising 'sstc' does not guarantee menvcfg.STCE is currently set. This creates the dependency chain: ISA string → has_sstc → direct stimecmp access, with no M-mode state verification.

findings.finding: bhyye hypervisor correctly sets henvcfg.STCE=1 when Sstc is available, enabling vstimecmp for VS-mode guests. This follows the spec requirement that HS-mode must set henvcfg.STCE to enable VS-mode stimecmp access. The code explicitly writes csr_write(henvcfg, HENVCFG_STCE) after checking has_sstc.
